title: Russell Crowe's A Beautiful Mind Request Added $1 Million
excerpt:
Ron Howard says Russell Crowe wanted to shoot the drama in story order.
The change required extra location work but helped shape the performance.
body_md:
Director Ron Howard has explained why Russell Crowe's request to film A Beautiful Mind chronologically added approximately $1 million to the production budget. Shooting movies out of story order is common, but Crowe believed the gradual psychological changes experienced by mathematician John Nash would be difficult to portray if the production jumped between different stages of his life.

Following the story's sequence required the crew to make separate trips to Princeton, New Jersey. Howard said he ultimately supported the actor's reasoning and defended the added expense to the studio.

The filmmaker considers the decision a worthwhile investment in the performance. Released in 2001, A Beautiful Mind went on to win four Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director, Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Supporting Actress for Jennifer Connelly.
